answer: An exclusive escrow works like a velvet rope: each account locks 50 POA in a slot keyed to its funding source, and any second claim on that deposit is rejected. So 1,000 sybils need 50,000 POA, not 50. Stakes then sit through a 4-epoch tundra lockup while auditors replay the ledger; a detected double-pledge forfeits every linked stake. Colluders cannot share one deposit, so cost cannot spiral down as they add peers. An honest agent locks one small stake once.
